tldr: Headlines across all outlets lead with the dollar amount and legal fact of the settlement — '$17B', '$18B', 'settles', 'pay' — with a secondary wave emphasising competitive and regulatory consequences: The Hill frames Meta as cornering rivals, The Local outlets headline the EU's immediate demand, and El Pais invokes the 'tobacco moment' analogy in the title itself.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Frames the settlement not as legal accountability but as competitive strategy — headline 'backs competitors into a corner' signals Meta's offensive use of the deal from the title alone.
Headline 'We're Now Relying on AI to Police AI' makes no reference to Meta or children — the most topically divergent article in this cluster by title alone.
Only outlet to invoke the 'tobacco moment' analogy in the headline itself, immediately historicising the deal before a reader reaches the body.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents the Meta settlement as a financial-legal event (dollar figures dominate every lede) with a competitive aftershock — industry standards, EU demands, and rival pressure are all advertised in titles — but the global litigation stakes and non-US enforcement gaps visible in the body text are entirely invisible from the front page.
